title: Lisse condensed cohomology on w-strictly local affines depends only on components
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $X$ put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use internal module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. A finite-rank lisse module means one locally isomorphic on a pro-etale cover to a finite free $\Lambda_X$-module, with rank allowed to vary [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Let $h:X'\to X$ be a morphism of affine schemes whose coordinate rings are w-strictly local [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Assume the induced map on profinite component spaces
$$\pi_0(h):\pi_0(X')\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_0(X)$$
is a homeomorphism, where components have the quotient topology [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite]. For every finite-rank lisse $\Lambda_X$-module $M$, the canonical pullback of derived sections is an isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(X,M[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X',h^*M[0])$$
in the ordinary derived category of abelian groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Here $R\Gamma$ is the total right derived functor of evaluation at the final object, followed by forgetting scalars; the displayed map is induced by the actual adjunction unit $M[0]\to Rh_*h^*M[0]$. It is natural in $M$ and in commutative diagrams of such morphisms, using the canonical pullback composition comparisons. No completeness, discreteness, Noetherianity, or extremal disconnectedness of the component spaces is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 4.1, Proposition 4.3, equation (4.2), and Corollary 4.7, extended by descent from w-contractible to w-strictly local affines using Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.2.8. This w-strictly local extension is agent-formulated, not a verbatim assertion of Proposition 4.3.

proof.text: Bundle the assumed component homeomorphism as e. Apply wstrict_common_component_hypercovers to f and e; the equality on component classes is the defining equation of connectedComponentsMap. Obtain the common profinite simplicial object S, the lifts U and V with all their matching covers and weak contractibility, and the face-compatible scheme maps g_n over f.

Fix a degree n. The lift data give affineness and w-contractibility of U_n and V_n and homeomorphisms eU and eV from their component spaces to S_n. The common profinite hypercover data give extremal disconnectedness of S_n. The equations for eU and eV on component classes and p(g_n(v))=q(v) show that g_n is an IsComponentLiftMap. Restrict the original lisse module to U_n using isLisseCoefficientModule_upperStar. Apply the lisse section comparison theorem at S_n and extract its bijectivity clause for that restricted module. This proves the displayed degreewise bijectivity hypothesis for every n, without making choices of coefficient data into public definitions.

Apply componentHypercoverUnitCriterion to U, V, g, their matching-cover witnesses, their weak contractibility, and the base and simplicial equations, using the bijections of the previous step. This proves invertibility of derived sections of the actual derived adjunction unit at M[0]. Unfold only componentLisseSectionsPullback and componentDerivedSectionsPullback. Its other two factors are the hom component of the terminal-section Leray isomorphism and derived sections applied to the hom component of the exact single-degree pullback isomorphism. Both are isomorphisms; their composite with the unit section map is an isomorphism.

Naturality in M is already encoded by componentLisseSectionsPullback. The separate theorem componentLisseSectionsPullback_comp is still unproved in Lean. Its intended proof is unchanged: the unit of the composite adjunction is the first unit followed by direct image of the second; the adjunction-compatible derived comparisons and section normalization identify composite and successive section pullbacks. Comparing two factorizations gives compatibility for commutative diagrams. Hypercovers only test invertibility and do not enter the definition of the canonical map.

proof_origin.place: HRS Proposition 4.3 and Corollary 4.7; existing compatible hypercover and lisse section comparisons, followed by the internal acyclic-hypercover unit criterion (Stacks Tag 09A2). The composition theorem remains open.
